why: Third round, from a real CI red: the consumer fault printed not_red because the tooling step had just run P1 and filled Vitest 5.0.5's file-system module cache, so the faulted run reused the cached resolution of @kalfa/config/App. The fault runner's two P1 runs now take their arguments from an exported consumerArgs that passes --fsModuleCache=false, and a D5 property pins it. The not_red refusal is unchanged.
note: The flag spelling was checked against the installed cac chunk, which lists fsModuleCache at top level; in a warm-cache tree both --fsModuleCache=false and --experimental.fsModuleCache=false made the faulted P1 fail, and the top-level one is used. Reproduction in a scratch git worktree with CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true FABRIKA_TEST_DEPTH=full after one plain P1 run: HEAD's related.ts gave not_red with the manifest restored; the fixed one gave faulted exit 1, rerun exit 0, restored digest equal, proven. The worktree was removed. No unit test warms the cache (it needs a package.json rewrite in a real install), so the reproduction is the evidence. related-selection 23 tests pass, pnpm lint exit 0, pnpm typecheck exit 0 (a pgrep -x tsgo seen right after lint was a transient; typecheck takes its own lock).
